text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Glafcos Clerides reshuffles his government. Officials call it an act of political renewal, the opposition says it is a sign of dismal failure.
- Heads roll for cabinet members from the Democratic Rally party. Four ministers are axed as Clerides shakes up his cabinet.
- Private money is to fund expansion in Larnaca marina.
- Offshore companies will be able to list on the Cyprus Stock Exchange.
- Bonds worth 25 million pounds are to be auctioned by the central bank.
- The result of failure. Clerides reshuffles his government.
- Belarus is to buy Cypriot wines and juices.
- A reshuffle with different messages. All political trends are represented in the new cabinet.

- Turks continue to provoke in Famagusta, firing across the ceasefire line into the free areas, while 28 Turkish fighter jets repeated their violation of Nicosia's flight information region on Monday.
- The cabinet resigned and four members of the Democratic Rally are out. All five ministers of the Democratic Party, the junior coalition partner, stayed.
- Cyprus Cement continues to be interested in acquiring control of Vassiliko Cement Works.
